A high wall of drum-hard wet sand, dark as chocolate and shovel-smoothed its full length, runs out of frame on both sides with only its middle section in shot. Fourteen bucket-cast turrets step away along its crown, each one showing the clean rib pattern of its casting. Three razor shells stand pressed into the near cut face at even intervals, point-first, plumb vertical. The innermost turret leans two degrees east and has begun to open a crack along its seam.

A fat round tower of packed wet sand, its flanks dark and tight, rises straight out of the bottom of the frame, its top course a fresh sharp-edged cylinder whose ribs are still razor sharp. Behind it, a double wall with a deep dry trench between its two faces runs away in both directions, the pale dry sand of the trench floor untouched. A mussel shell is pressed into the tower's near face at mid-height, tilted five degrees from true.

A wide canal cut crosswise, its near side a sheer wet face dropping full-frame from top to bottom, fills slowly with clear water that darkens the sand at the base of the cut. On the far side, nine bucket-cast turrets stand abreast, each one a different height, the tallest breaking the bright water behind them. At the canal's near edge, the cut face has begun to shed a thin stream of pale sand from one drying upper corner.

A staircase of eight linked pools steps down across the frame from the left edge to the right edge, both ends cropped, the bright water band lying along the top edge behind them, each pool a shade paler than the last as the wet drains away. The walls between them are low and wide, their tops smoothed flat. Two dozen flat pebbles are laid crosswise over the lowest dividing wall, pressed level into the wet sand. The second pool from the top is already half full and its far wall bows outward under the weight.

A gatehouse mass of packed wet sand, square-cut and broad-shouldered, fills the centre of the frame with its near face a sheer dark plane. A deep square-cut moat in front of it runs to both edges of the frame, its inner face vertical and its floor still wet and dark. Sixteen razor shells stand on end along the gatehouse crown, casting no shadow yet. A thin seam of pale dry sand has opened between the gatehouse base and the moat's inner face.

A ridge of two dozen drip-built spires stands packed across the frame, each one a different lean, the tallest breaking the bright water at the top of the frame. The spires at the near end are the darkest, still glistening, their flanks tapering to points no thicker than a shell edge. Behind them a low wide platform of smoothed wet sand spreads to the frame's far edge. One spire at mid-ridge has shed its top third onto the platform below.

A long spillway cut down the outer slope of a great packed mound runs crosswise across the frame from one side edge to the other, its floor pressed smooth and its sides cut clean and vertical. The mound's flanks rise steeply on both sides, their surfaces shovel-smoothed and dark. At the spillway's upper end, a notch cut in a dam crest is just wide enough to let water through in a thin moving line. Nineteen razor shells crown the dam crest on both sides of the notch.

A wall so high that the dozen bucket-cast turrets ranged abreast behind it show only their topmost rims above its crest runs from the left edge to the right edge of the frame without an end in sight. Its near face is a single shovel-smoothed plane of near-black wet sand. A whole line of mussel shells is pressed into that face in close rows, each shell tilted at the same angle, the lowest row at the base of the frame.

A canal splitting into two branches runs out of frame to the left and right, the island of packed wet sand between them rising dark and steep from both cut faces. The island's top is flat and smoothed, and a score of drip-built spires stand packed across it, each one leaning slightly toward the bright water at the top of the frame. The left branch is already full and still. The right branch is dry, its pale floor cracked in a fine net.

A whole outer face combed into close parallel grooves, each groove a shovel-blade deep and running the full height of the near wall, fills the frame from left edge to right edge. The grooves are dark and tight at their base and go pale and crumbly near the top where the sand is drying fastest. Behind the wall, three tall towers step away in staggered positions, the nearest one broad, the farthest one narrow, each casting its own dark stripe of shade across the grooved face.

A great packed mound with four switchback ramps cut round it fills the centre of the frame, the ramps dark and pressed smooth, each one a full bucket-rim wide. The mound's summit is flat. A range of tall thin drip towers stands along that summit's far edge, staggered in two rows, the rear row showing only its upper halves above the front row. Sand is still sliding in a thin pale stream from the mound's steepest uncut flank.

A dam of packed sand across a wide canal takes up the full width of the frame, its near face a vertical dark plane, its crest a smooth flat run with a spillway notch cut exactly at its centre. The notch is one razor-shell length wide. On either side of the notch, twelve razor shells stand on end pressed into the dam crest, point up, each one the same depth. Behind the dam the backed-up water is already touching the base of the farthest turrets.

A stretch of wall half its intended length ends abruptly at the right side of the frame in a fresh raw heap of dark wet sand still holding the rough shape of where it was tipped. The finished section to the left is shovel-smoothed and tight, with eight bucket-cast turrets ranged abreast along it from one side edge to the others crown, their rib patterns clean. The raw heap has begun to flow at its base, the lowest wet sand spreading in a thin dark tongue across the dry pale floor.

A whole quarter of the structure still only shallow scrapes cut in pale dry sand occupies the lower left of the frame, its intended outline a set of shallow irregular ditches that have not yet been deepened. Beyond that unfinished quarter, a high finished wall rises dark and packed, its near face a shovel-smoothed plane, with a row of flat pebbles laid into its crest crosswise at regular intervals. Where wet ends and dry begins, the sand shifts from near-black to the colour of chalk.

A tower leaning hard to the left, a crack running from its crown straight down one full face and widening at the base, fills the centre of the frame. Behind it and still intact, eleven more bucket-cast turrets step away along a low connecting wall, their flanks still dark and tight. At the base of the cracked tower, a fan of pale dry sand has spilled out where the crack has begun to let the interior drain. A single mussel shell is still pressed in above the crack.

A road of two dozen flat pebbles laid crosswise over a wide ramp runs from the bottom of the frame up to the crest of the wall at the top, each pebble a different grey-green, pressed level into the wet dark sand. The ramp's sides are cut clean and vertical. On the wall crest above it, four bucket-cast turrets stand abreast, their rib patterns still sharp. Between two of the turrets, the crest has been notched to a shallow V, and the notch is the only gap in the whole run.

A structure so long it runs out of frame on both sides without a visible end shows only its middle section: a wide flat-topped wall of drum-hard dark wet sand with a notched top, the notches cut at even intervals its full visible length. Behind it, two dozen drip-built spires stand pressed together in a dense cluster, the tallest of them breaking the bright water at the top of the frame, the shortest hidden behind the wall to their mid-point.

A whole flank carved into stepped terraces of dark packed sand, each terrace a flat wide shelf pressing into the frame from the left, runs from the bottom of the frame to the upper right where the bright water shows. The terrace edges are cut clean and sheer. On the lowest terrace, a run of eight linked pools has been cut crosswise, each pool separated by a low wall of smoothed wet sand. The nearest pool is full. The farthest is dry and already going pale at its edges.

An outer wall studded with pressed shells in close rows fills the near frame completely, its face a dark wet plane from which two hundred mussel shells project point-first, each one the same depth in, arranged in a grid with a shell-width gap between them. Behind that outer wall a second inner wall is visible above its crest, taller, with a line of razor shells standing on end along its own crown. Between the two walls, the dry pale floor of the trench is just visible.

A range of tall thin drip towers ranged across the frame in two staggered ranks, both running out of frame at both side edges fills the upper half of the frame, their bases planted in a wide flat platform of smoothed wet sand. The nearest row has seven towers, each one a different lean. The rear row has five, set in the gaps between those in front. The platform's near edge is a sheer wet cut face running the full width of the frame. A single razor shell stands point-up in that cut face, no taller than one drip tower's topmost knob.

A wall whose top is notched the whole way along at even intervals, thirty-one notches visible before it runs out of frame to both sides, rises from the bottom of the frame, its near face a single dark plane. Each notch is a clean square cut, one turret-height deep. Behind the notched crest, a great packed mound rises higher than the wall, its surface shovel-smoothed, and from its near slope a long spillway runs down across the frame from side to side, its floor pressed glass-smooth and still wet.

A tower whose top course is a fresh sharp-edged cylinder, its rib pattern still razor sharp and its sand still the near-black of something just cast, sits atop four older courses whose ribs have begun to blur as the sand dries to pale grey. A canal cut crosswise runs past the tower's base, its near side a sheer wet face. Pressed into that canal face at regular intervals, a line of flat pebbles projects like shallow ledges, each one a different warm tan, level and true.

A wall half its length with fresh sand still heaped where it was tipped at the right edge of the frame presses into the left side of the picture as a finished high dark run carrying eleven bucket-cast turrets along its crown. Between the finished wall and the fresh heap, a gap of one turret-width has been left open and the wet sand of the heap is already beginning to flow toward the gap, its leading edge a thin dark tongue on the pale dry floor.

A deep dry trench between two parallel walls runs crosswise through the full frame, its floor pale bone-dry sand and its two faces shovel-smoothed and vertical. The left wall is higher, with nine bucket-cast turrets crowning it, their shadows thrown into the trench. The right wall is lower and flat-topped, its crest packed with two dozen razor shells standing on end in a tight line, each shell a different height but all planted to the same depth, the tallest ones breaking the bright water above them.

A packed mound faced on its near side by a sheer dark vertical plane, its top carrying two rows of drip-built spires with the rear row taller than the front, fills the frame with no end visible to the left or to the right. At the mound's base on the left, a spillway notch has been cut through the lower wall, and pale dry sand from the mound's interior is streaming through it in a thin continuous fall onto the dark wet floor below. One drip spire on the front row has shed its top and stands blunt while the spires either side of it still taper.
